question_bank.question: A deep-research pipeline returns poor answers on some queries. What first diagnostic action best matches the lecture?
choices: Rewrite the final answer prompt immediately because visible errors usually come from the last stage.
Replace the web search provider first because retrieval failures are usually the largest bottleneck.
Inspect intermediate outputs for a set of bad queries before deciding which stage to change.
Train a larger model for every stage so manual analysis becomes unnecessary.
question_bank.explanation: The instructor recommends looking at intermediate steps on a sample of bad queries rather than guessing which component is responsible.

source_ref.evidence_span: just take a handful of queries.

frame_evidence.description: Whiteboard pipeline remains visible while the instructor explains manually checking query, search, fetch, and writing stages.

question_bank.question: What is the purpose of the spreadsheet the instructor suggests building during pipeline error analysis?
choices: To store generated reports so users can read them without rerunning the pipeline.
To record stage-by-stage judgments so failure hotspots can be counted across examples.
To replace manual inspection with random labels for each pipeline component.
To track training loss for one neural network rather than pipeline-level behavior.
question_bank.explanation: A spreadsheet makes the manual inspection systematic: each query can be checked by stage, and the counts reveal where failures concentrate.

source_ref.evidence_span: And so often, I would build a spreadsheet

frame_evidence.description: Instructor writes a table-like structure on the board with rows of queries and columns for pipeline steps.

question_bank.question: If the system fetches a low-quality backyard astronomy page instead of an authoritative NASA page, which pipeline stage is most directly implicated?
choices: The URL selection or fetching stage that chooses which search results to read.
The final writing stage that summarizes already selected evidence.
The user-query stage because the user should have asked a narrower question.
The model-size stage because all retrieval errors come from insufficient parameters.
question_bank.explanation: The example targets the stage that chooses which pages to fetch; the search may return useful pages, but the system selects the wrong one.

frame_evidence.description: Whiteboard notes show pipeline components while the instructor gives the Bob's backyard astronomy page versus NASA example.

question_bank.question: After reviewing many bad queries, what should the team do with the counts of where failures occur?
choices: Average them into one accuracy number and keep optimizing the final answer prompt.
Ignore the counts if the final output is unsatisfactory, because all stages are equally guilty.
Use the largest hotspot to choose the next subsystem for focused engineering work.
Discard queries with retrieval failures so the writing stage can be scored cleanly.
question_bank.explanation: The lecture's goal is to quantify failure hotspots. If one stage accounts for a large share of bad cases, that stage should drive the next engineering effort.

source_ref.evidence_span: Maybe 20% of the time, search terms are wrong.

frame_evidence.description: Instructor points at the board table where percentages are assigned to different pipeline failure modes.

question_bank.question: Why does the instructor say a few hours of manual pipeline error analysis can be high leverage?
choices: It guarantees that the first subsystem inspected will be the true bottleneck.
It makes the system fully automatic by removing humans from future evaluations.
It converts weak supervision into a supervised training set for every component.
It can prevent weeks of work on a subsystem that will not move the metric.
question_bank.explanation: Manual error analysis is costly but strategic: it can save far more time by preventing months of work on the wrong component.

source_ref.evidence_span: can save you weeks of otherwise heading in the wrong direction.

frame_evidence.description: Instructor stands beside the error-analysis table while emphasizing that the process saves misdirected engineering time.
